papers.title: Global Research Trends in Sleep Quality, Sleep Deprivation and Sleep Promotion Among ICU Patients: A Descriptive and Evaluative Bibliometric Analysis.
papers.abstract: Sleep deprivation and poor sleep quality are critical problems among intensive care unit (ICU) patients, with significant implications for recovery, delirium onset and clinical outcomes. Despite growing scientific interest, no bibliometric study has systematically mapped the intellectual structure and thematic evolution of this field. To analyse the bibliometric characteristics and thematic structure of publications on sleep deprivation, sleep promotion and sleep quality in ICU patients indexed in the Web of Science (WoS) database between 1983 and 2026. A descriptive and evaluative bibliometric analysis was conducted. Data were retrieved on April 26, 2026, from the WoS Core Collection using a comprehensive search strategy. Publications were filtered by document type, WoS categories (nursing, critical care medicine, anaesthesiology) and index (SCI-EXPANDED, SSCI, ESCI). Data were analysed using R software with the Biblioshiny interface, and annual publication trends were evaluated using Microsoft Excel. Of 11 418 publications retrieved, 379 met the inclusion criteria, spanning 37 years (1983-2026). Linear regression revealed a statistically significant positive trend in publication output (β = 0.643, R2 = 0.704, r = 0.839, p < 0.001), with mean annual publications of 10.24 ± 8.83 and notable acceleration from the 2000s onwards. Thematic mapping identified 'sleep', 'sleep deprivation' and 'delirium' as motor themes both highly central and well developed. Emerging concepts included circadian rhythm, actigraphy, fatigue, pain and anxiety. ICU sleep research has grown substantially over four decades, with sleep deprivation and delirium emerging as co-dominant research priorities. Thematic gaps and emerging clusters identified in this analysis highlight important directions for future nursing research and evidence-based practice development in critical care. This bibliometric analysis identified sleep deprivation and delirium as the co-dominant motor themes of ICU sleep research, and intervention-related concepts such as earplugs, eye masks and melatonin as emerging clusters. These evidence-based trends can guide ICU nurses in prioritizing targeted sleep promotion protocols and support policymakers in directing resources toward the most scientifically mature intervention areas in critical care.

papers.title: Facilitators and Barriers to Integrating Sleep Recommendations for Counselling Patients With Arthritis: A Survey of Physiotherapists and Students in Canada.
papers.abstract: Purpose: Individuals with arthritis face challenges in balancing activity, rest, and sleep. While physiotherapists address activity, sleep considerations are often overlooked, despite evidence suggesting better sleep improves treatment outcomes. The purpose of this study was to describe facilitators and barriers for physiotherapists and students incorporating sleep in practice. Method: We conducted a self-administered electronic survey among physiotherapists and students in Canada. The survey included 28 items (7-point Likert scale) mapped on the Capability-Opportunity-Motivation-Behaviour system and Theoretical Domains Framework. We report means (95% CIs) and identified facilitators (mean >5/7) and barriers (mean <4/7) by item. Results: Between January and November 2023, 216 responded and 191 (88%) completed the survey (149 physiotherapists; 42 students). Mean age was 35 (SD 11) years. Most delivered in-person care (67%) in urban settings (67%). Facilitators (mean >5/7) included the belief that sleep health is within practice scope, optimism about its benefits, awareness of sleep's importance in managing arthritis, learning about movement guidelines, and plans to integrate sleep education into arthritis treatment. Barriers (mean <4/7) included being unaware of where to find sleep resources (mean 3.63 [95% CI: 3.39, 3.89]) and lacking knowledge about sleep guidelines (mean 3.78 [95% CI: 3.46, 4.10]) and lack of confidence in guiding sleep for patients (mean 3.38 [95% CI: 3.10, 3.69]). Few reported providing sleep education for patients with arthritis (mean 3.52 [95% CI: 3.27, 3.77]), or observing similar behaviours from colleagues (mean 3.60 [95% CI: 3.40, 3.80]). Conclusions: While physiotherapists and students show positive perceptions about sleep health in practice, challenges remain for effective implementation. These findings can inform the development of theory-informed behaviour-change interventions to engage physiotherapists in greater sleep integration in practice.

papers.title: Loneliness, problematic digital media use, and nutritional-metabolic vulnerability in adolescents from single-parent households: an integrative review of eating- and sleep-related pathways.
papers.abstract: Adolescents from single-parent households may experience household time, economic, supervisory, and routine-related constraints that are relevant to psychosocial well-being, digital media use, eating behavior, sleep, and metabolic health. The objective of this integrative review was to synthesize evidence on the associations of loneliness and problematic digital media use with eating- and sleep-related behaviors in adolescents and to examine how single-parent household characteristics may influence these relationships. The review applies a contextual-behavioral vulnerability model in which household characteristics are treated as contextual modifiers; loneliness and problematic digital media use as the principal psychosocial and behavioral exposures; emotional eating, irregular meal timing, distracted eating, sleep disruption, circadian delay, and sedentary behavior as candidate intermediate processes; and diet quality, adiposity, and metabolic vulnerability as distal outcomes. Eligible evidence included peer-reviewed empirical studies, systematic reviews, and meta-analyses focused primarily on adolescents and examining at least one relevant association among family structure, loneliness, digital media use, eating behavior, sleep, energy balance, adiposity, or metabolic indicators. Studies explicitly analyzing single-parent households were treated as direct evidence, whereas broader adolescent or mechanistic studies were included when direct evidence was limited and were interpreted as indirect evidence. Direct single-parent evidence was concentrated mainly on family meals, screen-related routines, physical activity, and weight-related outcomes. Broader adolescent evidence associated loneliness with emotional eating and problematic digital media use with breakfast skipping, irregular meals, distracted eating, poorer diet quality, and sleep disruption. Evidence linking these behavioral patterns to adiposity, insulin sensitivity, circadian regulation, stress responsivity, and appetite-related signaling remained predominantly indirect and observational. Longitudinal, objectively measured, and biomarker-informed studies are needed to test these relationships directly in adolescents from single-parent households.

papers.title: The Thai version of the defense and veterans pain rating scale (DV-PRS) for postoperative pain assessment in patients after postpartum tubal ligation and total abdominal hysterectomy: a psychometric evaluation.
papers.abstract: Accurate postoperative pain assessment is essential for evaluating recovery. The Defense and Veterans Pain Rating Scale (DVPRS) is a multidimensional patient-reported measure assessing pain intensity and pain-related interference with activity, sleep, mood, and stress. Its psychometric performance has not been evaluated in Thai postoperative patients. This prospective psychometric validation study enrolled 288 women at a tertiary hospital in Thailand: 132 underwent postpartum tubal ligation within 24 h after vaginal delivery, and 156 underwent elective total abdominal hysterectomy outside the peripartum context. The DVPRS-Thai was administered at predefined perioperative time points. Evaluation included test-retest reliability, internal consistency, convergent validity against the modified Thai Brief Pain Inventory (mBPI-T), known-group validity, responsiveness, feasibility, and floor and ceiling effects. Preoperative test-retest rank correlations in the hysterectomy cohort ranged from ρ = 0.689-0.743, and internal consistency was high (Cronbach's α = 0.946). In the postpartum tubal ligation cohort, correlations with corresponding mBPI-T domains were moderate-to-strong (r = 0.55-0.84). Pain intensity and interference scores were significantly lower following postpartum tubal ligation than following total abdominal hysterectomy (all P < 0.001). Scores decreased significantly from postoperative days 1-3 after hysterectomy (all P < 0.001). Mean completion time was 3.4 ± 1.1 min. No ceiling effects were observed, whereas floor effects occurred primarily in supplementary interference items following postpartum tubal ligation. The DVPRS-Thai demonstrated satisfactory psychometric properties and feasibility in women undergoing postpartum tubal ligation or total abdominal hysterectomy; further validation across pain severities and other procedures is needed.

papers.title: Factors Associated with the Health Status of Caregivers of Community-dwelling Older Adults with Dementia in Japan: The Toyama Dementia Survey.
papers.abstract: Maintaining the health of caregivers providing home care for older adults with dementia is necessary. This study aimed to investigate the prevalence of physical and mental health problems among these caregivers and to identify the associated factors. The Toyama Dementia Survey, a county-wide cross-sectional study, was conducted in 2014. In the first stage, 0.5% of the total geriatric population (307,582 residents) in Toyama prefecture was randomly sampled, and 1,303 individuals who agreed to participate were selected. They were screened via face-to-face interviews, including memory tests. Among them, 252 (19.3%) were identified as having a high probability of dementia. In the second stage, home visits were conducted by psychiatrists and public health nurses. While psychiatrists diagnosed care recipients with dementia, public health nurses interviewed caregivers about their health problems. The analysis focused on 75 pairs of care recipients and their family caregivers who were visited. The association between behavioral and psychological symptoms of dementia (BPSDs) and the physical and mental health of family caregivers was examined using logistic regression analysis. Physical and mental health problems were experienced by 40% and 37.3% of the caregivers, respectively. The adjusted odds ratio (OR) for physical health problems among caregivers aged 80 years or older compared with those under 60 years was 13.46 (95% confidence interval [CI] 1.86-7.55). Compared with caregivers with patients without BPSDs, caregivers of patients with two or more BPSDs showed a marginal association with mental health problems (adjusted OR 2.96, 95% CI 0.84-10.43). Among physical symptoms, sleep deprivation was significantly more common in male caregivers than in female caregivers. Approximately 40% of caregivers of older adults with dementia experienced physical or mental health problems. Caregivers' age was associated with physical health problems. Male caregivers were more likely to experience sleep deprivation than female caregivers.
